SMTO-CFG-0024 — This conversation's settings changed in another window or device

GUID: 938c1e6d-d0d8-49cd-9cb1-82a24ca9c588
Slug: composer-revision-conflict
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • While you were changing a setting above the message box, the same conversation's settings were changed in another window or on another device. SMTO didn't save your change so it wouldn't overwrite theirs.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the page so the message box shows the conversation's latest settings. You'll see what was changed elsewhere before deciding what to keep.
  2. Check the mode, Target, Thinking and Output limit, then make only the change you meant to make. Redoing just your change keeps the other edits that were saved in the meantime.
  3. If SMTO is open in several windows or devices, close the ones you aren't using. Fewer open copies means fewer changes clashing with each other.

What success looks like

  • Your change is still there after you reload the page, and no error shows above the message box.

If it still fails

  • If it keeps happening, select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep selecting Retry settings in an old window; reload first so you don't undo someone else's change.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The composer profile change was rejected because expected_revision no longer matches the profile's current revision; another client saved a change first.

What this means

  • Composer patch expected_revision differs from the current profile revision inside its transaction. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • Composer patch expected_revision differs from the current profile revision inside its transaction.

How to diagnose it

  • Refresh current_profile and compare only the intended changed fields.

How to fix it

  • Re-read the conversation's composer profile, apply only the user's intended fields to the returned profile, and resubmit with its current revision as expected_revision. The desktop client already re-reads and retries once, so repeated conflicts point to another active writer.
  • Refresh this conversation’s current settings and reapply only the intended edit against the new revision.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A reviewed patch uses the current revision and preserves intervening unrelated choices.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
